practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 148 of the Indian Constitution provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG). He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

practiceQuestions.q: Who appoints the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG is appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of office for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
opts: 5 years or 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years fixed, with no age limit
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG holds office for a period of 6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the CAG submit his audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 151, the CAG submits his audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union to the President, who shall cause them to be laid before each House of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: By what process can the Comptroller and Auditor General of India be removed from office?
opts: By the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister
In the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court
By a simple majority vote in Lok Sabha
At the pleasure of the President
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG can be removed by the President only on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court (proven misbehavior or incapacity).

practiceQuestions.q: Who is known as the 'friend, philosopher and guide' of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament?
opts: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG acts as a guide, friend and philosopher of the Public Accounts Committee of the Parliament, examining the audit reports submitted by the CAG.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the post-retirement eligibility of the CAG under the Constitution?
opts: Eligible for reappointment to the same office
Eligible for appointment as a Union Minister
Ineligible for any further office under the Government of India or of any State
Eligible for appointment as Governor of a State only
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG is not eligible for any further office either under the Government of India or of any State after he ceases to hold his office, ensuring independence.

practiceQuestions.q: Where are the administrative expenses of the office of the CAG charged?
opts: Annual Budget allocated by the Ministry of Finance
practiceQuestions.sol: All expenses incurred in relation to the office of CAG, including salaries and allowances, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are not subject to vote of Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the CAG submit his audit reports relating to the accounts of a State?
opts: Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: The audit reports of the CAG relating to the accounts of a State are submitted to the Governor, who places them before the State Legislature.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Act enacted by Parliament regulates the duties, powers, and conditions of service of the CAG?
opts: CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
practiceQuestions.sol: Parliament enacted the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 to define the statutory scope of the CAG's authority.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the role of the CAG in India fundamentally differ from that of the Comptroller in the United States?
opts: US Comptroller has only audit powers, whereas Indian CAG has compilation powers.
US Comptroller has the power of prior disbursement control (no money can be drawn without approval), whereas Indian CAG has post-audit powers.
US Comptroller is appointed by the Judiciary, while Indian CAG is appointed by the Executive.
There is no functional difference; both exercise control over the exchequer before and after expenditure.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike the US Comptroller, who exercises ex-ante control (no money can be appropriated from the Treasury without their prior consent), the Indian CAG exercises ex-post control (auditing expenditure after it has been incurred).

practiceQuestions.q: In terms of the separation of functions in accounting and auditing, which of the following statements is accurate regarding the evolution of CAG's duties?
opts: The CAG is statutorily responsible for both accounting and auditing for both the Centre and the States since 1950.
The CAG was relieved of accounting responsibilities for the Central Government in 1976.
The CAG still compiles and maintains accounts for all States and Union Territories without exception.
The 1976 amendment completely abolished the auditing duties of the CAG over commercial undertakings.
practiceQuestions.sol: Originally, the CAG had the dual responsibility of maintaining accounts and auditing them at both Centre and State levels. In 1976, accounting was separated from auditing for the Central Government, relieving CAG of compilation duties for the Centre (though it still maintains state accounts in most states).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary objective of the 'Performance Audit' conducted by the CAG?
opts: To check only the arithmetical accuracy of government vouchers and receipts.
To evaluate whether government programs, schemes, and projects are achieving their intended objectives with economy, efficiency, and effectiveness (3Es).
To audit the private corporate sector receiving foreign direct investment.
To determine the tax rates for the upcoming financial year.
practiceQuestions.sol: Performance audit goes beyond traditional compliance and financial audit to examine whether government projects or policies achieve economy, efficiency, and effectiveness (the 3Es).

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution stipulate that the salary and service conditions of the CAG cannot be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment?
opts: To ensure absolute financial security for his retirement.
To guarantee independence from executive pressure or political influence while auditing public finances.
To maintain parity with the Chief Election Commissioner.
To comply with international auditing standards set by INTOSAI.
practiceQuestions.sol: Constitutional safeguards such as non-variable service conditions to his disadvantage are designed to insulate the CAG from executive coercion, ensuring fearless and objective audits.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the CAG audit the accounts of private bodies and non-governmental organizations (NGOs)?
opts: No, CAG's jurisdiction is strictly limited to government departments and PSUs.
Yes, if they receive substantial financial grants or loans from the government, subject to provisions of law or specific conditions.
Yes, but only under the direct orders of the Supreme Court of India.
No private body can ever be audited by CAG under any circumstance.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the 1971 Act and specific rules, CAG can audit receipts and expenditure of bodies and authorities substantially financed from Union or State revenues, including certain NGOs receiving government grants.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the relationship between the CAG and public sector undertakings (PSUs)?
opts: CAG has no jurisdiction over government companies or corporations.
CAG conducts direct audit of all PSUs, and commercial auditors cannot be appointed.
CAG can conduct supplementary audit of government companies whose accounts are first audited by private chartered accountants appointed by the Central Government.
CAG only audits the stock exchanges and RBI, leaving PSUs to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
practiceQuestions.sol: For government companies, the CAG's audit is supplementary. Commercial auditors (Chartered Accountants) are appointed by the Central Government on the advice of CAG, and CAG can conduct a supplementary audit of these accounts.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the CAG ensure transparency and accountability in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)?
opts: CAG directly audits every single village panchayat account in India annually.
CAG provides technical guidance and supervision (TG&S) over the maintenance and audit of accounts of PRIs and ULBs.
CAG has no constitutional or legal mandate regarding local bodies.
CAG audits local bodies only if requested by the Chief Minister of the State.
practiceQuestions.sol: Following the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, the Finance Commissions recommended, and the 1971 Act was amended, empowering the CAG to exercise Technical Guidance and Supervision (TG&S) over the audit of local bodies.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary reason why the CAG does not possess executive powers to penalize departments or officials found guilty of financial irregularities?
opts: Because CAG is an investigative agency subordinate to the Central Bureau of Investigation.
Because CAG is an independent auditing body meant to report to the legislature, maintaining separation of powers and legislative supremacy over the executive.
Because the Comptroller and Auditor General Act explicitly prohibits the CAG from interacting with bureaucrats.
Because financial irregularities are outside the purview of the Indian Constitution.
practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG's duty is to audit and report findings to the Legislature (Parliament/State Legislatures) through Public Accounts Committees. It is for the legislature and executive to take punitive or corrective action, preserving the watchdog's objective status.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following audit reports are submitted by the CAG to the President under Article 151?
opts: Audit report on Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts, and Public Sector Undertakings
Only the annual budget estimates of the Central Government
Only the performance appraisal reports of civil servants
Tax policy proposals for the upcoming financial year

practiceQuestions.sol: The CAG submits three audit reports to the President: Audit Report on Appropriation Accounts, Audit Report on Finance Accounts, and Audit Report on Public Sector Undertakings.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the CAG contribute to environmental governance and sustainable development auditing?
opts: By issuing environmental clearance certificates to industrial projects.
Through environmental and climate change audits, assessing government compliance with international commitments, pollution control funds, and sustainable resource management.
By levying carbon taxes directly on polluting industries.
By managing national parks and wildlife sanctuaries directly.
practiceQuestions.sol: Modern CAG audits include environmental audits (such as audits on water pollution, waste management, and climate funds) to evaluate whether government policies meet ecological and sustainability targets.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG):
1. The CAG is mentioned in Part V of the Constitution under Chapter V (The Comptroller and Auditor General of India).
2. The administrative expenses of the office of CAG, including all salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to or in respect of persons serving in that office, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 148 to 151 of Part V, Chapter V of the Constitution deal with the CAG. Article 148(6) states that administrative expenses of the CAG, including salaries and pensions of staff, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal and disqualification of the CAG:
1. The CAG can be removed by the President on an address from both Houses of Parliament passed by a special majority.
2. A person who has held office as CAG is eligible for appointment to any lucrative office under the Central or State Government after retirement if approved by the Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: CAG is removed in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge (special majority in each House of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehavior or incapacity). Statement 2 is incorrect because the CAG is strictly ineligible for any further office under the Government of India or any State after retirement.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the duties and powers of the CAG:
1. The CAG audits all receipts and expenditure of the Consolidated Fund of India, each State, and each Union Territory having a Legislative Assembly.
2. The CAG audits the accounts of any authority or body substantially financed from the Consolidated Funds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The CAG's mandate under Article 149 and the 1971 Act covers all receipts and disbursements from Consolidated Funds, Contingency Funds, Public Accounts, as well as bodies substantially financed by government revenues.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the reports of the CAG:
1. The CAG submits three audit reports to the President: audit report on appropriation accounts, finance accounts, and public undertakings.
2. The President lays these reports before both Houses of Parliament, where they are examined in detail by the Estimates Committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because CAG audit reports are examined in detail by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), not the Estimates Committee. The Estimates Committee examines estimates included in the budget.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the independence of the CAG:
1. The CAG is not a member of either House of Parliament, and his salary cannot be altered to his disadvantage during his term.
2. The conditions of service of persons serving in the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and the administrative powers of the CAG are prescribed by the President in consultation with the CAG.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under Article 148, the conditions of service of persons serving in the department and administrative powers of CAG are prescribed by the President after consultation with the CAG.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of CAG to audit commercial enterprises:
1. The CAG audits government companies in accordance with the provisions of the Companies Act.
2. The CAG has statutory authority to audit the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the State Bank of India (SBI), and the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. CAG audits government companies under the Companies Act provisions (supplementary audit). By specific statutory provisions, CAG also audits bodies like RBI, SBI, LIC, and other statutory corporations.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the evolution and scope of CAG's audit functions:
1. Originally, the CAG's audit was restricted to financial audit and regularity audit, but over time it has expanded to include propriety audit and performance audit.
2. Propriety audit empowers the CAG to examine whether public spending has been done with wisdom, faithfulness, and economy, looking beyond mere legality of expenditure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Propriety audit allows the CAG to look into cases of waste, extravagance, and lack of wisdom in public expenditure, even if the expenditure is legally sanctioned.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding secret service expenditure and the CAG:
1. Secret service expenditure incurred by intelligence agencies is completely immune from any form of audit by the CAG.
2. The CAG cannot call for vouchers or particulars of secret service expenditure and must accept a certificate signed by the competent administrative authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because secret service expenditure is not completely immune from audit; it can be audited under special confidential arrangements. Statement 2 is correct: the CAG cannot call for detailed vouchers of secret service expenditure but accepts a certificate of expenditure signed by the competent authority.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of the CAG:
1. The CAG is designated as the guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system of the country at all levels.
2. The CAG ensures that no public money is spent without the sanction of the Parliament, functioning as an ex-ante controller of funds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. While CAG is called the guardian of the public purse, he does NOT control the financial system of the country nor does he act as an ex-ante controller (he exercises post-audit control after expenditure is incurred, unlike the UK or US systems). Money can be drawn from the Consolidated Fund without CAG's prior approval.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the interaction of CAG with State finances:
1. The CAG submits his audit reports relating to the accounts of a State to the Governor of that State, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature.
2. The Governor can direct the CAG to audit the accounts of any body or authority not statutorily covered under the 1971 Act, after consulting the CAG and obtaining state legislative approval.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct (Article 151(2)). Statement 2 is incorrect because under Section 20 of the 1971 Act, the President (for Central bodies) or Governor (for State bodies) can entrust the audit of any other body to CAG with the prior approval of the President/Governor, but it does not require prior state legislative approval in that manner, and specifically, the Governor acts with concurrence or consultation as per statutory guidelines.
